doc.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Learning by copying, then finding your own identity
summary: Influence is fine but one should develop a personal sound, like learning to drive then driving your own way.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: In other words, it was okay to be influenced by somebody, and okay to try and do some of what they did conceptually, but not note for note.

Yeah. Definitely. And another something too is now in order for me to learn how to drive a car, I have a take instructions from you and do what you do. But after I learn how to drive then I drive my own way. So that’s what they always said. You know you might have to copy somebody in order to learn how to articulate or how to phrase well, you know, if you see somebody you like. But after that, after you learn that, then get your own thing so that people will say, this is so and so. And then you’ll have your own identity.
